subject: Creating a Legend Manually Below A Plot

messages.author: e04bb64c7c0b4424
messages.subject: Creating a Legend Manually Below A Plot
parts:
Hi All, 

I am attempting to use the scatterplot3js library because the rgl package currently has a fatal error in it with the most recent version of Shiny and R. I am not quite sure why, but the developer hasn't gotten around to fixing it on cran. This question was asked in May and he seems to be unwilling to adjust the repository at this time. I can't use the workaround solution he provided because I am behind a company server and can only pull from the most current cran repository due to our strict security policies. 

So I have to use a new library. Scatterplot3js is fairly new and I have it up and running. Unfortunately, this library doesn't have any ability to add a legend (at this point). I was wondering how I could go about dynamically generating some list of colored text below the plot that would act as a basic legend until the developer actually adds this feature. (he is very active with the code so it shouldn't be more than a month or so)

I think I could do this with  a renderHTML function that has a renderText within it. I would do this so that I can add however many lines of text I need dynamically. Unfortunately,  I have been playing around with the idea but I am not getting very far on it just yet.  Is there a better way to go about this in Shiny? 

As a side note, I understand it is bad practice to manually do this, but I am on a very tight time schedule and need a "bandaid" solution. It is a poor excuse, I know.

Thanks for your time and help, 

Amber

messages.author: e04bb64c7c0b4424
messages.subject: Re: Creating a Legend Manually Below A Plot
parts:
As an update, I was able to get the code working. It does what I asked, it just looks a bit ugly. If anyone has any suggestions for this please let me know. 



        output$threeDText<- renderUI({
            x<- div("PLOT 3D LEGEND", style = paste0("color: black"))
            col<- unique(values$threeDColors)
            for(i in 0:length(col)){
              x<- list(x, div(values$combinedGroupChosenData[i], style = paste0("color:",col[i])))
            }
            return(x)
        })


Thanks,

Amber
